To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the partitioning behavior of PAP and BR was determined by the presence of highly exposed positively charged residues (Arg, Lys and His) and tryptophans (Trp) in BR, respectively.
the partitioning of papain and Bromelain, two cysteine-proteinases, in aqueous two phase systems (ATPS) was studied.

(i) the differential behavior of PAP and BR in aqueous two phase systems (ATPS) could be explained by a different charge transfer interaction between the proteins and the polyethylen glycol (PEG) molecules, which is favored for BR, and (ii) the presence of highly exposed positively charged residues (His, Arg and Lys) and tryptophan residues in BR molecule would explain this behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the partitioning behavior of two cysteine-proteinases in ATPSs and the molecular determinants that explain the differential distribution of both biomolecules in these systems.
the study of partitioning behavior of PAP and BR, two well known cysteine proteases.
the molecular features determining different partition patterns in aqueous two phase systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BR is a highly charged protein with exposed tryptophan residues and PAP is a highly hydrophobic protein.
the different molecular features of both proteins, such as the presence of highly exposed Trp and Lys residues in BR, would be responsible for the observed partitioning behavior.
the different partitioning patterns observed for PAP and BR in the assayed ATPSs are determined by the molecular surface properties of the biomolecules, and not by the charge or molecular weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the partitioning behavior of a protein in ATPSs is not only determined by its molecular weight and isoelectric value, but also by the presence of highly exposed charged and aromatic residues in the protein surface.
PEGs of high molecular weight (2000 and above) are the most adequate to partition both enzymes in ATPSs.
PEGs with high molecular weights (4600 and 1000), and low polymer concentrations (4% w/w) would be the best conditions to obtain a high partition coefficient for PAP in aqueous two phase systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the partition behavior of cysteine-proteinases in aqueous two phase systems is determined by a combination of molecular features that are not necessarily related to the charge or the size of the biomolecule.
PAP and BR can be separated in ATPSs formed by PEG 600 and PEG 1000, respectively, by taking advantage of their differential partitioning pattern.
the partitioning behavior of proteins is determined by their specific molecular features.
